svg.title: What ExpandRetrieveJob reads, changes and returns
svg.desc: Read-only inputs, the context it changes in place, local scratch state, the return value, and the external side effects some job methods have.
svg.metadata: ["The declaration: a context pointer, the job's payload id and its job_index go in; a stdx::Expected<void, JobFailure> comes out. That is all the signature tells you.", "Read-only inputs flow in: Scheduler members (layout_, motion_graph_), the job's fields, ctx->initial_state and the keep-out filters, read through the const ctx->FindKeepOutFilter().", "Inside, the method builds a local working_state: a copy of initial_state with the existing events applied (ComputeStateAfterPlannedEvents). Its edits (e.g. setting the bay to READY_TO_RETRIEVE) touch only this copy.", "The shared PlanContext is read and written through ctx while the method runs: before this first job, ctx->event_dag and last_event_by_entity are empty.", "After the call: four new events (all job_index 0), five edges and three last_event_by_entity entries. This is the real output, and none of it appears in the return type.", "The return value only reports the outcome: {} on success, or a JobFailure {message, is_retryable} so Dispatch can keep a job that cannot run yet. On failure Plan() restores the context it copied before the job, so the job's events go too.", "Some job methods also reach outside the plan: ExpandInsertJob sends a bay-reset request to Dispatch during expansion, and Plan() fires clean_garage_request_fn_ on an INSERT failure.", "A sketch of a pure alternative (not in the code): return the events, edges and follow-up requests as a value and let Plan() commit them, so the signature shows everything."]
